Synopsis:
    Indian state-run and private companies are shifting to longer-dated bond issuances (10–15 year and perpetual) to meet strong structural demand from insurers and pension funds, driven by liability-matching needs and growing investible corpuses. The shift is partly tactical: hawkish RBI commentary has pushed up short-duration corporate yields, compressing the relative appeal of near-term borrowing. Simultaneously, reduced supply of long-dated sovereign and state-government paper has tightened spreads on long-duration corporate bonds to 18-month lows. Some market participants caution this is not a structural shift but a situational absorption by specific investor types.
